item.title: DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement. The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers. Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. The alert said investigators have seen the stolen assets converted primarily into ether. A separate $400 million deepfake scheme, and 900 seized videos Separately from the DOJ and Binance case, the U.S. attorney’s office in the Central District of California and the FBI announced the seizure of cloud-based infrastructure used in a social engineering campaign the FBI is calling FaceStealer. item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After a Fresh Session Low as the 10-Year Yield Holds Above 5%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After a Fresh Session Low as the 10-Year Yield Holds Above 5% Bitcoin price traded near $71,200 on Thursday evening, after slipping to a fresh session low near $71,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. U.S. stocks closed modestly lower and the 10-year Treasury yield held above 5% after Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. The decline started in the morning. Bitcoin price fell below $72,000 before the opening bell and dropped to about $71,150 shortly after 10 a.m. Eastern. A bounce later faded, and the bitcoin price printed a new session low near $71,000 around 6:23 p.m., its weakest level since Aug. 20. It now stands roughly $30,400 below where it closed one year ago. Stocks close lower as yields keep pressure on the bitcoin price The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.39% to 25,366.09, the S&P 500 lost 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.36% to 52,297.09, Reuters reported. Nvidia shares finished 4.3% lower at $166.19, off the day’s lows, after the company said Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and a board member, effective immediately, and named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Bitcoin-linked stocks had a harder session. Strategy (MSTR), which MSCI is removing from its USA Index at the Nov. 30 close, finished at $114.41, down 6.5%. Shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which had bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows through Wednesday, closed at $40.36, down 4.5%. The bond market did much of the afternoon work. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 12 basis points to 5.105% and reached 5.12%, its highest since Oct. 21, after President Donald Trump said the United States does not need a deal with Iran, Reuters reported. The two-year yield, which tracks Federal Reserve expectations most closely, climbed about 14 basis points to 4.867%. Brent crude settled at $95.82 a barrel, up 3.3%, after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalated. Fed hike bets, a $404 billion deficit and a busy evening of crypto news Higher yields reflect a market that still expects the Fed to tighten again next month. Fed funds futures are pricing in 29 basis points of hikes in December, a quarter-point move as the base case with only slim odds of a half-point step, Reuters reported. Rising rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and that has weighed on the bitcoin price all week. The Treasury added a fiscal reminder after the close. The government ran a $404 billion deficit in October, the first month of fiscal 2027, the Treasury Department said , up 42% from $284 billion a year earlier, as receipts fell to $369 billion and outlays rose to $773 billion. Some benefit payments that would normally have been made on Nov. 1, a Sunday, were shifted into October. The evening also brought a cluster of crypto headlines. item.title: Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares Jane Street Group raised its Strategy (MSTR) stake 53.8% in the third quarter, to 4,119,097 shares, a Form 13F filed Thursday shows, a position dated to Sept. 30 that does not capture any trades the firm may have made since then. Those caveats matter as much as the increase. Jane Street is a trading firm, and one of the largest market makers in stocks, ETFs, and options, and the same filing lists call options covering 13,573,000 Strategy shares and put options covering 13,991,800 shares, each more than three times the size of the common stake. Some of that stock is likely a hedge for the options and market-making book rather than a straight bet on the company. The 13F does not say how much. The shares were valued at $630.6 million in the filing, using the Sept. 30 price of $153.09. Strategy has fallen about 25% since then. At Thursday’s close of $114.41, the same 4,119,097 shares were worth about $471 million. The Class A position is up 1,441,475 shares from the 2,677,622 Jane Street reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at $232.8 million. The firm filed about four days ahead of the Nov. 16 deadline; the SEC accepted the report at 4:04 p.m. Eastern on Thursday. Call and put positions that dwarf Strategy’s stock The options lines were already large in the second quarter and grew again. Calls covering 13,573,000 shares were valued at $2.08 billion in the new filing, and puts covering 13,991,800 shares, listed in two rows, were valued at $2.14 billion. Those figures use the same Sept. 30 share price as the common-stock line; a 13F reports the underlying shares the options cover, not the cash premium paid for the contracts. The report is a holdings filing that folds in positions across seven other included managers, among them Jane Street Capital, Jane Street Options and Jane Street Global Trading, so the Strategy lines can include inventory across the group rather than a single proprietary bet. Authorized Signatory Jeremy Kahn signed the report in New York on Nov. 12. The table lists 14,764 entries valued at $1.19 trillion. Other early 13Fs so far, with bigger names still to file Jane Street’s 53.8% increase was the sharpest percentage increase among the large Strategy stakes in Thursday’s early 13F wave. Capital International Investors, a Capital Group unit, raised its stake 4.5% to 36,467,109 shares, worth about $4.17 billion at Thursday’s close. Invesco added 10.9%, to 10,362,698 shares, worth about $1.19 billion. Renaissance Technologies cut its position 41%, to 1,515,560 shares, worth about $173 million, and left the spot bitcoin ETF holdings it had reported at midyear, including BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust. JPMorgan Chase, in a filing already reported , lifted its Strategy stake 36% to 848,932 shares and held 11.4 million IBIT shares, worth about $460 million at Thursday’s close. item.title: DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals. Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work. Individual cases point to Monero and bitcoin The closest official window into how the vendors were paid comes from the cases the Justice Department highlighted and from court papers posted with the announcement. Alexander Green, 32, of Jacksonville, North Carolina, was arrested in June and charged in the Southern District of Ohio with conspiracy to distribute controlled substances, including fentanyl. The department said he allegedly operated a vendor called STARLABS on DrugHub, which it described as a Monero-only dark web market, and that the group has been linked to two overdose deaths. A criminal complaint says undercover purchases from STARLABS were made “in exchange for cryptocurrency.” If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison. In a separate Florida arrest, brothers Stanislav Chernyshov, 30, and Vladislav Chernyshov, 35, are charged in the Eastern District of Virginia with conspiracy to distribute Schedule I synthetic opioids. item.title: Peter Schiff on the Bitcoin Crash: “Get the Hell Out”
item.description: ▶ Bitcoin Magazine Peter Schiff on the Bitcoin Crash: “Get the Hell Out” Challenged on why two or three down years would matter for Bitcoin when gold and the Nasdaq have had similar streaks before recoveries, Peter Schiff says the difference is the backdrop. When a market can’t go up on the best news it has ever had, he argues, that normally indicates that it’s going to go down. He calls Bitcoin “all hype,” with no intrinsic value, income, or dividends, and says much of the supply now sits with ETF investors and Bitcoin treasury companies rather than people who want to use it as money. All of that hot money, he warns, is going to exit, the market will go down faster than it went up, and he expects a massive washout. Even long-term bulls, he says, will have cheaper opportunities after leveraged speculators are cleared out, and he adds that this is not the time to be hodling. item.title: Binance Says It Has Fully Covered the $6.34 Billion Hack With Company Funds
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Has Fully Covered the $6.34 Billion Hack With Company Funds Binance said Thursday it has completed coverage of the $6.34 billion Oct. 29 hack from company funds, two weeks after the largest crypto theft on record, even as withdrawals continue to reopen in phases. In a Thursday announcement, the exchange wrote that it “has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident” and published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot. It repeated the same message on X. That wording matters. Coverage means Binance has replaced the affected tokens from its own books, not that it has recovered the stolen coins from the attackers. The exchange said it committed more than $6.34 billion in company funds and bought the affected tokens through market and over-the-counter channels, drawing on a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of its futures insurance fund above the level required under its risk-management framework, and its corporate treasury. Binance has also committed to replenishing SAFU to about $1 billion after that partial draw, a step it said would keep the fund fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve. A very small number of tokens the exchange no longer lists were also affected. Binance said those holdings will be handled under its delisting process and that users who hold them will be covered. A wider proof-of-reserves snapshot, but no independent check yet Binance took a new proof-of-reserves snapshot at 00:00 UTC on Nov. 12, or 7 p.m. Eastern on Wednesday, covering 198 tokens. That is a sharp jump from the 10 tokens included in the Oct. 31 snapshot published in the days after the breach. The new figures are now posted on the exchange’s proof-of-reserves website. The snapshot, Binance said, “provides an updated view of assets that are fully accounted for.” Users cannot yet check that claim themselves. The exchange said the full zero-knowledge proof will take about 40 to 50 hours to generate because of the computational workload. After that, users holding the affected tokens “will be able to independently verify that their assets are backed at a minimum of 1:1.” Until the proof is ready, the 1:1 backing is Binance’s statement, not something customers can confirm on their own. Withdrawals are still coming back in phases Thursday’s update does not reopen the platform all at once. Binance said it continues to reopen withdrawals in phases and will share further details once they are confirmed. The exchange first reopened withdrawals on Nov. 1, starting with bitcoin and then expanding to other networks, and has kept the restart on a phased timetable since then. The announcement also does not say how much of the stolen assets have been retrieved, and it does not name an attacker. Covering customer balances leaves that recovery question unanswered. item.title: Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26 Israel Discount Bank said Wednesday that from Nov. 26 it will let eligible customers buy, hold and sell bitcoin and ether in the bank’s mobile app, a launch that would beat larger rival Bank Leumi if it stays on schedule. The Tel Aviv-listed lender described the service as a first for Israel’s banking system in a Nov. 11 statement. Customers will be able to trade the two assets alongside stocks and bonds, without opening an account at an outside exchange or managing a separate digital wallet. The offer is limited to private, not corporate, customers who are Israeli residents, 18 or older, and whose accounts are already set up for securities trading, subject to the bank’s terms. “For the first time in the banking system, Discount Bank will allow trading in digital currencies directly from the bank account in a simple and secure manner, without the need for complex dedicated digital wallets,” Avi Levi, CEO of Discount Group, said in the statement. “This is a first step toward establishing advanced technological infrastructure in the digital currency space and developing the bank’s capabilities in this area.” The rollout was led by Elad Fisher, head of the bank’s financial markets division. Coins will sit in bank-provided wallets built on infrastructure from Fireblocks. JUST IN: $150 billion Israel Discount Bank will become the 1st bank in Israel to let customers buy, hold and sell Bitcoin Adoption! pic.twitter.com/gwKBy17cSf — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 11, 2026 A 2% commission and a wallet that does not leave the bank The bank’s product page lists a 2% commission on purchases and sales in the app, not including any foreign-exchange conversion. Custody fees are waived for six months from the Nov. 26 launch and then run 0.25% a quarter. Trading is open Sunday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 11 p.m. Israel time, and only immediate orders are allowed. Customers can buy as little as 0.01 of a coin. Holdings appear in the securities portfolio at once, with cash settling the next business day in U.S. dollars; conversion into shekels happens only if the customer asks. The service is a closed system for now. Bitcoin and ether bought through Discount cannot be sent to an outside wallet, and coins held elsewhere cannot be transferred in. The bank said it may revisit transfers later. It also warns of unusual risk, high volatility and the possibility of a total loss, and says the coins are not legal tender and lack the same protections as securities. What Discount is selling, besides convenience, is tax treatment. Capital gains and losses on the coins can be offset automatically against the rest of the customer’s investment portfolio for tax withheld at source, the bank said, at a 25% rate on profits.
